entries.location: Hogwarts — summer recollection
entries.description: Harry recalls the castle’s secret passages and ghosts, Great Hall banquets, a four-poster in the tower dormitory, Hagrid’s cabin next to the Forbidden Forest, and six tall Quidditch goalposts.
entries.model_notes: A narrated recap reaffirming established features; no new floor plan or numeric goalpost height.

entries.location: School cabbage cultivation
entries.description: Hagrid says flesh-eating slugs are ruining the school cabbages and that he is buying repellent.
entries.model_notes: Establishes school cabbage-growing and a pest problem, without identifying a bed, greenhouse or location beside Hagrid’s hut.

entries.location: King’s Cross — sealed school gateway
entries.description: The usually traversable barrier between platforms nine and ten becomes solid to Harry and Ron after the other Weasleys pass through. Their trolleys collide, pushing does not open it, and no train sound is audible through the cold metal.
entries.model_notes: Remote school-transport access state; its cause is not yet known. The gateway is concealed from Muggle sight.

entries.location: Railway and flying-car approach
entries.description: The boys follow the Hogwarts Express north, using the car’s compass and repeated checks. Fields give way to purple moors, villages and a large city; later the railway winds past a snow-capped mountain.
entries.model_notes: North is the observed journey heading, not a castle facade bearing. No city or mountain is named.

entries.location: Castle cliff and lake — aerial view
entries.description: Hogwarts’ many towers and turrets silhouette the horizon on a cliff above the lake. The car approaches over the smooth black water, described as a mile below, with the castle ahead.
entries.model_notes: Mile refers to an aerial separation estimate at that moment, not the height of the supporting cliff.

entries.location: Aerial crash route — castle wall to Willow
entries.description: The descending car almost hits a dark stone castle wall, turns in an arc over dark greenhouses, then a vegetable patch, then black lawns, and hits a thick tree trunk.
entries.model_notes: Explicit ordered overflight; no compass side, spacing or proof that the cabbages occupy this particular patch.

entries.location: Whomping Willow
entries.description: The ancient gnarled tree bends its trunk almost double and strikes the car with twisted branches, thick boughs and knucklelike twigs. Its roots creak as it reaches after the reversing car, and its branches continue flailing after escape.
entries.model_notes: The name comes from Snape’s later identification. Reach and trunk size are relative; no numeric safety radius established.

entries.location: Whomping Willow — collision damage
entries.description: Snape reports considerable damage to the old valuable Whomping Willow after the car collision.
entries.model_notes: Reported damage without itemised broken branches; car dents do not establish corresponding tree wounds.

entries.location: Whomping Willow vicinity to front entrance
entries.description: After being ejected onto damp ground, the boys drag trunks up a grassy slope towards the huge oak front doors, leaving luggage at the foot of the front steps.
entries.model_notes: Confirms a lower crash area relative to the entrance approach; no distance from Willow to doors.

entries.location: Great Hall — exterior window sightline and sorting
entries.description: From a brightly lit window near the front steps the boys watch sorting inside the Great Hall: hovering candles above four long tables, golden plates and goblets, the starry ceiling, and a stool for the Sorting Hat before the first-years.
entries.model_notes: Exterior visibility of Hall interior is a significant constraint. No window side, sill height or exact angle is given.

entries.location: Entrance Hall to Snape’s office
entries.description: Snape takes them up the steps into the vast torchlit echoing Entrance Hall, then down a narrow stone staircase into the dungeons, opening a door halfway along a cold passage to his office.
entries.model_notes: Office door is halfway along this passage; passage length and dungeon level are not specified.

entries.location: Snape’s office — jars, desk and hearth seating
entries.description: Shelves of large specimen jars line the shadowy walls. A large slimy object in green liquid stands on a shelf behind the desk. The initially empty fireplace is lit by McGonagall’s wand, and two chairs stand beside it.
entries.model_notes: Office distinct from Potions classroom; a usable hearth and desk-relative specimen shelf are observed.

entries.location: Snape’s office — conjured supper
entries.description: McGonagall produces sandwiches, two silver goblets and iced pumpkin juice on Snape’s desk; the sandwich plate refills as the boys eat.
entries.model_notes: Temporary office meal service, not a permanent catering installation.

entries.location: Snape’s office to Gryffindor Tower
entries.description: The return route passes murmuring portraits and creaking suits of armour, climbs narrow stone stair flights and reaches the passage containing the Fat Lady’s oil painting in a pink silk dress.
entries.model_notes: Adds stair materials, sounds and portrait medium; no complete turn-by-turn map.

entries.location: Gryffindor common room — password and tables
entries.description: The new password Wattlebird opens the portrait onto the crowded circular common room, whose furniture includes lop-sided tables and squashy armchairs.
entries.model_notes: Furniture shapes are observed during a temporary welcome crowd; password dated to this arrival.

entries.location: Gryffindor second-year dormitory
entries.description: A door across the common room leads to a spiral stair. Climbing right to its top reaches the same circular dormitory as last year, now signed second-years, with five red-velvet-hung four-posters and high narrow windows. Trunks stand at bed ends.
entries.model_notes: Same cohort retains the room while its sign changes. Right to the top describes this route at this time; tower-storey count remains unspecified.

entries.location: Great Hall — cloudy ceiling and Howler acoustics
entries.description: The ceiling mirrors a dull grey cloudy sky over the four breakfast tables. Ron’s Howler fills the Hall with amplified sound, rattling tableware, echoing from stone walls and shaking dust from the ceiling.
entries.model_notes: Observed acoustic and ceiling behaviour; no sound-pressure level or ceiling construction inferred.

entries.location: Castle, vegetable patch, greenhouses and Willow
entries.description: The pupils leave the castle and cross the vegetable patch to the greenhouses. From outside the greenhouses, the Willow is visible in the distance with several branches in slings; Sprout approaches across the lawn carrying bandages.
entries.model_notes: Adds ground route and sightline; sling damage state dated after the car crash.

entries.location: Greenhouse Three — access and hanging flowers
entries.description: Sprout unlocks Greenhouse Three with a large belt key; pupils have previously worked only in Greenhouse One. Three contains more dangerous plants, damp earth and fertiliser smells, and strongly perfumed umbrella-sized flowers hanging from the ceiling.
entries.model_notes: At least separately numbered One and Three exist; numbering alone does not describe greenhouse Two. Door is lockable.

entries.location: Greenhouse Three — teaching bench and Mandrakes
entries.description: A trestle bench stands centrally with about twenty pairs of coloured earmuffs. Deep trays hold roughly a hundred purple-green seedling Mandrakes in rows; pots are stored under the table, with more pots and sacks of compost available. Four pupils work to each tray.
entries.model_notes: Layout and safety equipment for the repotting lesson; quantities are approximate.

entries.location: Greenhouse Three — hazardous plants
entries.description: The Mandrake earmuffs block all sound; Sprout says seedling cries cause hours of unconsciousness while mature cries are fatal. A spiky dark-red Venomous Tentacula extends long feelers towards her and withdraws after a slap.
entries.model_notes: Sound blocking and Tentacula response are observed; cry hazards are taught by Hermione/Sprout, not tested on pupils.

entries.location: Courtyard — stone step and side-door route
entries.description: After lunch the pupils go into the courtyard, where Hermione sits on a stone step and voices echo. Lockhart takes Harry into the castle through a side door, down a corridor and up a staircase to his classroom.
entries.model_notes: Links courtyard side entrance to an ascending classroom route without a floor number; class bells are audible outside.

entries.location: Defence classroom — furniture and window relation
entries.description: Lockhart’s classroom has pupil desks, his desk at the front, wall pictures, ink bottles, a waste bin, a window by the back rows, and a ceiling candelabrum. He places a large covered cage on his desk.
entries.model_notes: Window proximity inferred directly from the back row showered with glass, not a measured window-wall plan.

entries.location: Defence classroom — pixie damage
entries.description: Released Cornish pixies shatter a window, spray ink, shred papers and books, tear pictures from walls and overturn the bin, throwing objects outside. Neville hangs from the candelabrum, which later gives way, dropping him. Pupils shelter beneath desks; remaining pixies are immobilised and recaged.
entries.model_notes: First-lesson damage state; no repair timing is supplied.

entries.location: Castle to Quidditch stadium — dawn route
entries.description: Harry descends the dormitory spiral stair, crosses the common room, exits the portrait hole and leaves the castle for dew-covered grass and sloping lawns down to the stadium changing rooms.
entries.model_notes: Reaffirms downhill pitch route; dawn mist and birdsong are seasonal scene conditions.

entries.location: Quidditch changing room — seating and tactics boards
entries.description: Players sit on opposite sides of the changing room with a wall behind one side; Wood presents three boards of pitch diagrams, with coloured arrows animated by a wand tap.
entries.model_notes: Seating is observed without a specified bench form. Portable tactical boards do not fix pitch shape beyond the text.

entries.location: Quidditch stadium — high seats and sound
entries.description: Colin occupies one of the highest spectator seats; his camera clicks sound strangely amplified across the otherwise deserted stadium. Players fly round the stadium and a corner.
entries.model_notes: Corner wording alone is insufficient for a rectangular field or square stands.

entries.location: Stadium to Hagrid’s hut — nearby refuge
entries.description: Harry calls Hagrid’s the nearest place to take Ron. They leave the stadium, cross the grounds towards the Forest’s edge, and hide behind a nearby bush within twenty feet of the cabin when Lockhart emerges.
entries.model_notes: Observed route and bush proximity; nearest is Harry’s judgment, not a measured comparison with hospital distance.

entries.location: Hagrid’s cabin — corners, table and basin
entries.description: The one-room cabin has an enormous bed in one corner and a crackling fire in another. Chairs surround a scrubbed table used for tea; Hagrid brings a large copper basin for Ron.
entries.model_notes: Adds separate bed/fire corners and table finish; rooster and basin are temporary objects.

entries.location: Hagrid’s rear vegetable patch
entries.description: A small vegetable patch behind the cabin contains about a dozen boulder-sized pumpkins being grown for the Hallowe’en feast. Hagrid’s pink umbrella leans against the cabin’s back wall.
entries.model_notes: Pumpkins receive admitted magical help; Hermione proposes an Engorgement Charm. This patch is not automatically identical to the castle-to-greenhouse vegetable patch.

entries.location: Hagrid’s cabin to Entrance Hall
entries.description: The pupils walk back uphill to the castle and enter the cool Entrance Hall before proceeding into the Great Hall for lunch.
entries.model_notes: Confirms castle above hut approach; no path material or precise distance.

entries.location: Trophy room — silver and named awards
entries.description: Ron’s detention involves polishing silver trophies without magic. He later reports repeatedly cleaning the Quidditch Cup and a Special Award for Services to the School.
entries.model_notes: Named displayed awards and polishing; Ron’s estimate of a hundred cups is not an exact inventory.

entries.location: Lockhart’s office — second floor and photographs
entries.description: Harry reaches Lockhart’s office along the second-floor corridor. Many candles light countless framed photographs of Lockhart on the walls; another large pile of photographs lies on his desk.
entries.model_notes: Explicit office floor, desk and candlelit self-portrait decor; office is separate from classroom.

entries.location: Lockhart’s office — unexplained voice
entries.description: During detention Harry hears a venomous disembodied voice while Lockhart says he hears nothing. The office otherwise contains candle sounds and Lockhart’s speech.
entries.model_notes: Dated acoustic event, not proof of an invisible occupant or of a door opening; source route unresolved at this point.

entries.location: Grounds and castle — prolonged autumn rain
entries.description: Damp chill enters grounds and castle. Days of heavy rain thunder on the windows, raise the lake, turn flowerbeds into muddy streams and swell Hagrid’s pumpkins to garden-shed size.
entries.model_notes: Flooded planting beds and lake rise are seasonal, with no numeric level change.

entries.location: Dungeon five — ceiling mess
entries.description: Nick reports that third-years plastered frog brains over the ceiling in dungeon five and that Filch has been cleaning it.
entries.model_notes: Named/numbered dungeon, not identified as the usual Potions room.

entries.location: Upper corridor tapestry route to Filch’s office
entries.description: Filch emerges through a tapestry on Harry’s right in a corridor with a window, then takes him downstairs to his office. Harry later leaves the office along a corridor and climbs back upstairs.
entries.model_notes: Relative floor change only; tapestry suggests concealed circulation but no passage destination is independently mapped.

entries.location: Filch’s office
entries.description: The office is dingy and windowless, with a low ceiling supporting a single hanging oil lamp and a faint fried-fish smell. Wooden filing cabinets line the walls; a desk with drawers and quill/ink containers faces a wall display of polished chains and manacles. A moth-eaten chair stands beside the desk.
entries.model_notes: Punishment records occupy labelled cabinets, including a drawer for Fred and George. Ceiling-hanging punishments remain a reported request, not current practice.

entries.location: Classroom over Filch’s office — damaged cabinet
entries.description: A loud overhead crash rattles Filch’s lamp. Back upstairs Harry sees the wreckage of a large black-and-gold cabinet in a classroom; Nick says he had Peeves crash it directly above the office, and Filch calls it a valuable vanishing cabinet.
entries.model_notes: Observed wreckage plus reported identity and cause. No paired cabinet, transport destination or later repair inferred.

entries.location: Gryffindor common room — salamander fireworks
entries.description: A fire-dwelling orange salamander smoulders on a table among armchairs before the twins’ firework makes it whirl about the common room shedding sparks and orange stars; it escapes into the hearth with explosions.
entries.model_notes: Temporary magical disturbance; no lasting furniture damage is stated.

entries.location: Great Hall — Hallowe’en 1992
entries.description: The Hall is decorated with live bats and huge pumpkin lanterns, large enough for three men to sit inside. Golden plates and candles glitter at the packed feast; dancing skeleton entertainment is only rumoured.
entries.model_notes: Pumpkin scale is explicit but not numeric; keep the skeleton troupe unconfirmed.

entries.location: Great Hall approach to Deathday dungeon
entries.description: At seven the trio pass the Great Hall doorway and head down towards the dungeons. The party passage is lined with thin black candles burning blue; temperature drops along it. A corner leads to a doorway draped in black velvet.
entries.model_notes: A roomier dungeon is the reported venue. No dungeon number or relation to Snape’s office is supplied.

entries.location: Deathday dungeon — dance floor, orchestra and chandelier
entries.description: Hundreds of translucent ghosts crowd a dance floor. An orchestra of thirty musical saws performs on a black-draped platform; a chandelier holds a thousand black candles with midnight-blue flames. The dungeon is cold enough to mist the pupils’ breath.
entries.model_notes: Party installation includes a podium in an icy-blue spotlight and wall-penetrating ghost horses. No physical stable or horse-access door is required.

entries.location: Deathday dungeon — food table
entries.description: Across the dungeon a long black-velvet-covered table holds rotten fish on silver platters, burnt cakes on salvers, maggoty haggis, mouldy cheese and a tombstone-shaped anniversary cake. Ghosts pass through the table and food to try tasting them.
entries.model_notes: Temporary olfactory and table arrangement; ghost permeability does not imply walk-through solid surfaces for people.

entries.location: Myrtle’s girls’ toilet — floor and disrepair report
entries.description: Hermione identifies Myrtle’s haunt as the girls’ toilet on the first floor, out of order all year because Myrtle’s tantrums flood it.
entries.model_notes: Preserve this reported first-floor placement; reconcile separately with subsequent journey descriptions rather than silently changing it.

entries.location: Deathday dungeon to second-floor writing corridor
entries.description: Leaving the dungeon, the trio return up the candlelit passage towards the Entrance Hall steps. Harry follows a voice apparently moving upward, climbs into the Entrance Hall, up the marble staircase to the first floor, then another flight to the second; he runs round that floor to its last deserted passage.
entries.model_notes: Floor sequence explicit. Sound source travelling through ceilings is Harry’s hypothesis; no phantom route is established.

entries.location: Second-floor writing corridor — windows, torches, water and cat
entries.description: Foot-high warning words about the Chamber’s opening shine on a wall between two windows in torchlight. A large puddle covers the nearby floor; Mrs Norris hangs stiffly by her tail from a torch bracket beneath the writing. After the feast, pupils reach this passage from both ends via stairs.
entries.model_notes: Dated attack state with two-ended circulation, windows and bracket; no ink material, window spacing or exact stair count.

chapter_reviews.notes: Complete chapter read; Hogwarts recap retained. Privet Drive house and garden are outside boundary scope.
Complete chapter read, including the dream. Dobby’s warning describes no specific Hogwarts space or physical boundary; off-site confinement excluded.
Complete chapter read. Burrow, rescue flight and generic comments about house-elves in castles supply no new Hogwarts or nearby-boundary description.
Complete chapter read. London shops, Floo route and Burrow excluded from castle-boundary model; Hagrid’s school-cabbage report retained.
Complete chapter read. Imagined triumphant landing excluded as imagined; actual overflight order, external Hall sightline, dungeon office and retained dormitory recorded.
Complete chapter read; greenhouse numbering, layout, hazardous plants and classroom damage retained. No greenhouse material or fixed classroom floor invented.
Complete chapter read. Kept Hagrid’s rear patch distinct from the main vegetable patch. Advice about kelpies in a well does not locate a well at Hogwarts.

Complete chapter read. Recorded first-floor Myrtle report and explicit second-floor attack route separately; no silent floor reconciliation. Vanishing cabinet identity and overhead cause labelled as reports.
